first_impression.reaction: Googled 'rhodes wedding venues' with three planners open in a spreadsheet. The intro splits the island into four areas and says it comes down to guest count, ceremony and setting. No fluff, so I kept going. I went to the FAQ first, then the table, which says it isn't a ranking and admits the gaps. Only one venue out of nine publishes a capacity, and the page says so straight out. That's honest, even if it's not much to go on. I read the legal and weather sections properly. Two spots where the copy says more than its own data shows: Rodos Palace and the west coast 'suiting a larger guest list', and an Old Town FAQ that never actually answers the question.

journey.quote: Grande Albergo delle Rose in Rhodes Town is the only venue here that publishes a reception figure, with seating for 450 guests.
journey.reaction: Good. It tells me how thin the published data is instead of padding it out. One real number, and they admit it's the only one.

journey.section: Rhodes wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: It is not a ranking. "Not published" means the venue does not state the detail.
journey.reaction: No made-up 'number one'. A table with blanks in it is more believable than a perfect one.

journey.section: Rhodes wedding venues at a glance
journey.reaction: Then the Elysium section says it 'lists wedding receptions and vow renewal ceremonies'. So is it receptions only or not? Small thing, but it's the sort of mismatch I notice.

journey.quote: House rules that a venue does not publish, from capacity to minimum nights, are confirmed in writing by your Wedded Advisor before you commit, so [book a Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=rhodes-wedding-venues&utm_content=primary) once you have a shortlist.
journey.reaction: Pitch before I've read a single venue profile. 'In writing' is the right message, so it's minor, but the proof should come first.

journey.section: Choosing an area of the island
journey.quote: It suits a larger guest list that wants everything on one property.
journey.reaction: Based on what? The table says Rodos Palace's wedding capacity is 'Not published'. Conferences aren't weddings. That's a claim the page's own data doesn't back up.

journey.quote: The wedding coordinator provides a schedule, a costing sheet with deadlines, an outline of costs and an itinerary, and meets the couple on arrival.
journey.reaction: A costing sheet with deadlines. That's what I want from anyone handling my money. Useful detail.

journey.quote: Extras at a supplement run to fireworks, a Greek music group with dancers and a DJ until 3am or later.
journey.reaction: It says 'at a supplement'. So they're not pretending the package covers everything. That's where the upsell normally hides.

journey.quote: Because of its popularity, it needs to be booked as far in advance as possible, so lock the chapel before anything else if it is the setting you want.
journey.reaction: A real constraint and a clear action. Good.
The 3,000 events are conferences and incentives. Using that as wedding scale when the wedding capacity isn't published is a stretch. Same issue as the west coast line.

journey.quote: The figures below come from the [Hellenic National Meteorological Service](http://oldportal.emy.gr/emy/en/climatology/climatology_city?perifereia=South%20Aegean&poli=Rodos) Rodos station, data period 1955-2010.
journey.reaction: Named source, named station, date range, then a proper table. Exactly how I'd want it.

journey.quote: Wildfires occur from June to September, including near tourist areas on the islands, and can start with little warning.
journey.reaction: Heat, fires, lifeguards, Saharan dust. Most wedding sites leave all of this out. Points for it.

journey.section: Getting legally married on Rhodes, in brief
journey.quote: Ceremonies at the Town Hall of Rhodes take place every Wednesday and Friday, and the couple return to the registry office the next working day to sign and have the marriage certificate drawn up.
journey.reaction: A specific, checkable detail I'd never have known. That 'next working day' bit matters if guests are flying out.

journey.section: Getting legally married on Rhodes, in brief
journey.quote: The embassy does not provide legal advice, and the onus is on you to present documents in the correct form.
journey.reaction: Honest about the limits. No pretending it's all handled for me.

journey.quote: Plan the Old Town as your portrait setting.
journey.reaction: I asked whether we can get married in the Old Town. Is that a yes or a no? It sounds like a dodge. Give me the straight answer first, then the advice.

journey.section: Shortlist your Rhodes venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Right signal. Still doesn't tell me whether the venues pay you too, but I'd ask that on a call.

unanswered_questions: Can we legally marry inside the walls of the Old Town or not? The FAQ doesn't say yes or no.
Does Rodos Palace actually take a large wedding, or is that inferred from its conference business?
Does Elysium host wedding ceremonies, or only receptions and vow renewals?
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from any of these venues? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real Rhodes wedding with the actual budget I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: It suits a larger guest list that wants everything on one property.
turn_offs_found.why: The table lists Rodos Palace's capacity as 'Not published'. Saying it suits a larger guest list is a claim the page can't support. Conference history isn't wedding capacity, and once I spot one of these I start doubting the rest.
It turns 3,000 conferences and incentives into wedding credibility. Minor, because the venue's own figure is stated, but the framing does more than the facts allow.

turn_offs_found.quote: Plan the Old Town as your portrait setting.
turn_offs_found.why: It's a direct question with no direct answer. Steering me to 'portraits' without saying yes or no reads like the page is avoiding the catch.

turn_offs_found.quote: House rules that a venue does not publish, from capacity to minimum nights, are confirmed in writing by your Wedded Advisor before you commit, so [book a Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=rhodes-wedding-venues&utm_content=primary) once you have a shortlist.
turn_offs_found.why: A CTA before any venue is described. The message is fine, but the pitch comes before the proof.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the at-a-glance table and the area overview
My dad, the heat, wildfire and dust paragraphs and the legal section with the Wednesday and Friday Town Hall detail

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start your shortlist with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=rhodes-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The page mostly earned it. It admits the gaps, gives one real capacity figure, names supplements and booking constraints, and dates its weather and legal facts. What holds me back is the Rodos Palace 'larger guest list' line and the Old Town non-answer, where the copy goes further than its own facts. And I'd still want to know whether you take a cut from the venues.

top_3_changes: Must-fix: remove or soften the Rodos Palace capacity inference. 'It suits a larger guest list that wants everything on one property' (west coast area) and 'Experience at scale' (Standout) suggest wedding scale, but the table lists capacity as 'Not published'. Reword to what's supported, e.g. a resort with its own conference centre where the whole stay can sit on one property.

Must-fix: give the Old Town FAQ a direct answer. 'Can we get married in Rhodes Old Town?' opens with 'Plan the Old Town as your portrait setting.' Lead with a plain yes or no that the source pack supports, then the advice.

Reconcile Elysium: the table says 'Not published; receptions only' and the body says 'Elysium Resort & Spa lists reception spaces only', but the venue section says it 'lists wedding receptions and vow renewal ceremonies'. Make them match. Optional: move the primary CTA below the first venue section so the evidence comes before the pitch.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and table first, cross-checked claims against the page's own data, looked for catches and upsells
No invented brand facts; commission and real-budget questions placed in unanswered_questions as deferred
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored
Title, deferred business details and absence of prices not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or 'not published' explanations

open_questions.question: Does the source pack support a direct yes/no on marrying inside the Old Town walls? If not, the writer could reword the FAQ question itself rather than give an indirect answer.

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'rhodes wedding venues' while comparing three planners; Rhodes is one option among several, hence relevance 4.
No prices on the page is deliberate and not penalised.
Venue self-descriptions attributed to the venue (e.g. Kallithea Springs 'one of the most popular') are not counted as the brand's own unsupported claims.
Title is person-set and deferred, so not flagged.
